body:
# Independent sketch signoff — 2026-10-07

Both specs independently require sketch changes. No implementation, tests, grants, statuses, holds or merge performed. No operator authority floor altered.

CHANGES REQUESTED — BUG-1802 independent sketch review

Reviewed independently against main 199e591b07aa76a59cd34f0a41946f918501f6ba. This session did not author the sketch or implementation. Authority-changing final merge remains the operator's. This is a sketch verdict, not a code-review approval or permission to implement the unresolved design.

Verified evidence

Read AGENTS.md, two-seat protocol, rework/recovery discipline, aida-orchestrate sketch gate, full spec/comments through /home/joe/ai/aida/target/agent/aida, both sketch files and SKETCH_AUTHOR_READY.md. CLI reports 0.15.0, build 199e591b07+dirty; inspected tracked source matches the pinned commit. The old bug-1802-review-independence branch at b409b5ae3ebb7c6e1e354d5ee77492d1f048ef32 has only 93 added template lines relative to its merge base; untouched. TASK-1599 did not implement this fix.

lib.rs::review_recorded_by_from (96318) really uses missing name/type to assign operator attribution. handle_review_record_at (95825) writes protection, verdict, markers and events without authenticated review identity. stamp_pr_review_verdict (9486) substitutes a drain string. pr_ship::approval_head_refusal/open_approvals/approved_match_head, pr_cmd::ship_refusal_release and merge_hold::refusal_release consume verdict/head evidence without the requested identity validation. merge_gate_verdict_candidates also silently drops unreadable/unparseable files: adding only a field validator after that filter would leave a missing-approval bypass.

Existing identities are not interchangeable: SessionLease.id (lib.rs:33377), SeatGrant.session_id (seat_authority.rs:17), SessionManifest.session_id/claude_session_id and AgentRegistryEntry.id/native_session_id/resumed_from. OrchestratedLeaseReceipt (lib.rs:106723) already joins conversation, lease, branch and worktree; it has no grant/spec UUID/head attribution and recover_lost_child_state removes a partial receipt. Registry GC and manifest pruning also preclude assuming those are permanent evidence. current_grant validates the immediate parent, not an arbitrary complete ancestor chain. require_direct_human checks TTY and two managed-agent environment markers; it does not authenticate absence of an agent against persistent launch identity.

Binding answers to sketch questions A–E

A. Approval requires a valid reviewer/advisor grant or a direct-human TTY path, with actual identity and independence established before writes. No role/name-string fallback. Reject an implementer grant, the same durable implementation actor/session (including resumed/reissued identity), or a reviewer whose ancestor is an implementation actor for this work. Two distinct children of a nonimplementing driver are allowed; common OS user/principal or common driver ancestry alone is not self-review. Traverse validated ancestry with cycle/missing-record refusal; current_grant alone does not establish that property. A TTY plus missing environment strings cannot override positive managed-session/implementation evidence. Keep existing emergency hold placement intact.

B. Prefer extending and retaining existing launch/session/grant evidence plus the existing review JSON rounds. Do not mandate a new global provenance ledger, broker, requirement format or duplicate authority store. The minimal necessary join is canonical repository + spec UUID + reviewed-work lineage -> all relevant implementation actor/session identities -> retained grant/launch evidence, and independently reviewer actor/session -> its valid recording authority. A display ID, lease owner, git email, PR author or latest lease alone cannot supply this join. The exact producer/retention/coverage design is the blocker below; this answer does not bless the sketch's unspecified new binding.

C. Keep historical closed verdicts, refusals, findings, retained rounds and closure evidence readable and untouched. Legacy approvals cannot authorize new shipping. Fresh review alone does not repair unknown implementation identity: re-review can authorize only when retained evidence actually establishes independence. Missing evidence refuses with its precise gap. No automatic backfill or new human attribution-repair override is authorized. Target-scoped, valid fresh rounds can supersede old rounds under existing ordering; unrelated historical legacy records must not poison every future PR.

D. Validate authority at recording and retain that evidence so normal time expiry/process exit does not erase a valid review. Explicit revocation (reviewer or relevant ancestor) blocks subsequent use for an unmerged target; historical closed work stays closed. On this baseline role_cmd::handle_role_end calls revoke_current: it is explicit revocation under this conservative rule, even if used as routine logout, so it can require re-review before shipping. Do not silently reinterpret revoked_at as harmless cleanup. Missing/corrupt references or ambiguous ordering refuse. No new retroactive invalidation or bypass command is required.

E. The supported-workflow/local-grant boundary is sufficient for this bug; no same-Unix-user tamper-resistance claim. A protected broker would require separate architecture/operator direction. No roster/grant/human-floor expansion is authorized here.

Required sketch revision before signoff

1. Name the existing record(s) to extend, exact minimal added fields and retention owner, and every producer/consumer symbol. Provide a concrete sequence for interactive pickup, standalone headless, orchestrated phase, direct session/agent launch, resume, rework, role reissue and session cleanup. Identify where the implementation actor becomes bound to the actual reviewed branch/head and how the complete relevant author set is established. A launch record containing an initial head is not proof of authorship of later commits. Unknown coverage must refuse; a fresh session cannot wash away a prior implementation identity. Show how uninstrumented/legacy changes are detected instead of accepted as an empty author set. Do not code a broad ledger to paper over this unresolved join.
2. Specify canonical target resolution, retained-record validation and serialization at publication/consumption. Carry an explicit invalid/missing/corrupt candidate result through merge_gate_verdict_candidates; never filter an untrusted approval into the existing no-review-required case. Apply the same check at ship preflight and under the merge lease, drain merge matching, corpus/rework-release paths and reviewer handshake ingestion. --override-stale-approval cannot override bad identity. Drain transport may annotate CI but cannot manufacture reviewer proof or inherit a prior round's proof. Specify ordering that prevents a concurrent refusal from being erased and canonical publication failure from clearing a marker.

Required named witnesses (proposed tests, not executed)

Keep the sketch's real-CLI review_record_implementer_cannot_self_approve_cli, review_record_independent_granted_reviewer_cli, review_record_direct_human_tty, review_record_identity_survives_cleanup_and_rework, ship_rejects_untrusted_review_provenance_entrypoint and ship_rechecks_provenance_under_merge_lease. Add review_record_reissued_grant_same_actor_refused; ship_malformed_approval_is_not_no_review; drain_review_transport_cannot_authenticate_child_json; ship_revoked_review_refuses_but_expired_review_retains_record_time_authority. Drive actual review record / pr ship and production drain phase/merge entrypoints with fake forge/vendor and isolated HOME, including refusal-release, canonical/local conflicts, retained archive, valid sibling reviewer, head movement and concurrent refusal. Unit parser tests alone cannot witness this fix. Preserve closed legacy history in a fixture and prove it is not rewritten/reopened.

Disposition: CHANGES REQUESTED for the concrete identity/coverage and gate-publication design above, not for a new operator policy decision. No blanket block on BUG-1808. Revision returns to an independent advisor; no status/queue/hold/grant changes or implementation authorized by this verdict.

---

CHANGES REQUESTED — BUG-1808 independent sketch review

Reviewed independently against main 199e591b07aa76a59cd34f0a41946f918501f6ba using /home/joe/ai/aida/target/agent/aida for full BUG-1808 and TASK-1337 specs/comments. This session did not author the sketch or implementation. Final authority-changing merge remains operator-owned. Source inspection only; no live pickup reproduction or tests executed.

Verified evidence

TASK-1337 is present and must remain: queue_cmd::handle_queue_work (10936 onward) resolves role and branch before synthesized-row/calibration/setup writes, but validate_child_delegation is guarded by !no_launch && !no_human. resolve_queue_work_plan uses role_hint for fallback while synthesis/head selection still consult shell role. QueueCommand::Work dispatches batch/nextN/auto-complete before ordinary pickup. session::spawn_vendor_headless_with_seat and spawn_claude_headless_resume issue late child grants; exec_vendor_headless does not. Existing task_1337_delegation_refuses_before_any_pickup_mutation, task_1337_held_branch_refuses_before_any_pickup_mutation and task_1337_post_setup_launch_error_prints_manual_guided_continuation are real CLI tests; assert_pickup_unstarted checks status/session files/queue membership, not the full acceptance snapshot.

The proposed assignment shortcut is not established by the cited helpers. orchestrator_authorizes_explicit_queue_pickup_with_token checks a live token and shared DrainState.current; it does not join the calling grant/session to that token's member. orchestrator::read_live_run checks live parent/member PIDs and marker.spec membership, but RunMarker has no child-grant identity. lib.rs::run_implementer builds a queue-work subprocess, phase environment and lease receipt, then uses spawn_and_wait_watched (or pane hosting); the inspected path does not itself issue an implementer grant. Plain headless later inherits the environment. Therefore neither a live token nor calling this path an 'already-issued phase child' proves a scoped child grant was issued. Multi-member runs also cannot rely solely on shared current.

Binding answers to sketch questions A–E

A. Yes: --no-launch/TUI setup mutates the listed lifecycle state and must preflight the routed role. A caller-minted --session-id is not authorization. Require real delegation for launcher setup; permit same-assignment execution only with corroborated scoped assignment and valid actor identity. Dry-run/list remain nonmutating. Preserve TASK-1337's ordinary post-authorization vendor-failure manual continuation.

B. A genuinely already-issued scoped phase child executes its assignment without recursively delegating to itself. Verify canonical root, token-specific live member/spec, actual phase/seat, and a retained binding to this caller's grant/session; reject mismatched, stale or missing proof. The existing helpers are useful corroboration, not a complete join. A launcher, including inherited driver-authority headless execution, must validate delegation and install the routed child authority before running vendor work. It cannot run implementation using the parent driver's authority. Specify one issuance owner per path so resume/reviewer wrappers do not issue a second child from a nondelegating child. The exact binding/issuance call graph is a blocker below.

C. Unchanged-state acceptance includes late authority refusal; no narrower acceptance is approved. A concurrent peer's legitimate changes remain, but this refused invocation must leave none of its own lifecycle changes and must never restore old whole-file state over a peer. A residual-state diagnostic is honest failure reporting, not acceptance compliance. No broad transaction rewrite or speculative 'CAS compensation' is signed off.

D. Preflight all statically required seats for the actual selected mode/variant and bounded initial members before run/admission writes; check dynamically admitted members before their admission writes. Do not require seats for phases that will not run. Retain TASK-1603's register-before-status/launch ordering after authorization succeeds. A whole long-running drain is not rolled back after already authorized earlier members executed; each later admission/launch still needs its own safe refusal boundary.

E. Explicit --role controls non-review selection consistently, including no-arg head and synthesis, while PR/MR scope keeps its documented reviewer rule. Print selector/selected role separately from validated launcher authority. Suggest an authorized launcher select the routed role; never suggest changing role as an automatic authority remedy. None of these decisions grants advisor/product/integrator delegation absent their actual valid grant and roster.

Required sketch revision before signoff

1. Provide a per-entrypoint sequence naming QueueCommand::Work wrappers, handle_queue_work, run_auto_complete/run_implementer, standalone reviewer, fresh/resume spawn, rework direct call and TUI setup. State whether each is a launcher or an assigned consumer; identify the precise grant issuance and token/member/session binding writer and validator. Do not substitute environment flags, RunMarker.spec alone or shared DrainState.current for caller assignment. Name any minimal additions to existing records; preserve successful assigned-child execution without recursive delegation or widening its delegation set.
2. Choose one bounded final-validation/publication mechanism and specify it concretely. Inventory first writes (queue, canonical spec/history/calibration, fetch/refs/FETCH_HEAD, dormant cleanup, worktree/branch, lease/manifest, reviewer-file reset, grant and orchestration records). For staging, name staging paths, publication point, lock order, which authority/roster and lifecycle writers honor those locks, expiry handling and crash recovery. For compensation, name each existing CAS/ownership predicate and writer API, how canonical status/history changes are undone without fabricated history, and what happens when a peer changes the same artifact. Queue row equality or a standalone queue lock cannot atomically restore spec/history, refs and worktree state. An append-only status event is not undone by simply changing status back. Authority check then issue_child after setup is exactly the race requiring a design, not its solution. Keep unrelated cleanup/pull side effects outside an operation that promises unchanged state unless their effect is explicitly covered. Do not assume the existing grant writer/roster writer share a transactional lock: inspected seat_authority has no such locking protocol.

Required named witnesses (proposed tests, not executed)

Retain all three TASK-1337 integration tests. In aida-cli/tests/queue_work_dry_run.rs extend the fixture snapshot and add bug_1808_headless_delegation_refusal_is_atomic; bug_1808_explicit_selector_does_not_change_launcher_authority; bug_1808_all_entrypoints_preflight_before_mutation; bug_1808_preflight_races_fail_closed; bug_1808_assigned_phase_is_not_recursive_delegation. Name actual argv for interactive/guided, headless fresh, supported resume, standalone reviewer, --no-launch with TUI session id, batch, nextN, auto-complete, and rework path. Use a real CLI and production phase launcher with fake vendor/forge and isolated HOME/AIDA_HOME. Include queued and implicit rows, pre-existing InProgress state, readied caches, no-vendor sentinel, and full lifecycle snapshots. Place deterministic barriers after planning, before first write and immediately before final issue/launch; revoke/expire/change roster and race a peer update there. Prove no child, no invocation-owned residue and preserved peer edits. Add valid nondelegating assigned-child success, wrong-member token refusal, inherited-driver grant refusal/scoping, and no extra child issuance in resume/reviewer paths. Source-string checks alone are insufficient.

Disposition: CHANGES REQUESTED for concrete assignment binding and atomicity, independently of BUG-1802. Existing acceptance determines the conservative answers above; no operator acceptance relaxation is assumed or requested. If a revision proposes allowing late-refusal residue, that is a separate operator choice: retaining strict acceptance requires the atomic design; relaxing it would permit partial setup and change the requirement. Current work must use the strict choice. Return the revised sketch to an independent advisor before implementation; no status/queue/hold/grant changes authorized here.

## Publication

Verdicts saved locally; canonical spec comments and advisor notification pending.
subject: Independent sketch verdicts: BUG-1802 and BUG-1808 require changes
